findings.claim: getActivePlanName is queried unconditionally alongside hasAnySubscription, but isOfferedToSpace only uses its result when hasEverSubscribed is true, so for every never-subscribed workspace this SELECT executes and its result is discarded. This should either be folded into a single subscription query returning both exists and planName, or resolved conditionally only when hasAnySubscription is true.

Every POST /checkout-url call now performs the full offer computation (general catalog fetch, space-specific catalog fetch, three DB queries, plus the checkout POST itself); the three DB queries run on every checkout attempt even though the catalog reads are cached, which could be costly if checkout is a hot path. A lighter-weight assertOffered(paymentLinkId, spaceId) that reuses cached catalogs and short-circuits DB reads could be considered.

warnOnUnclassifiedTrials fires on every call to listOfferedPaymentLinks, meaning every GET /payment-links and POST /checkout-url request for the same misconfigured catalog logs the same warning, which could flood logs with repeated messages under a bad configuration. Logging at debug/rate-limited warn per link id with in-memory dedup, or moving the check to a catalog-refresh path so it only warns when the datasource actually re-fetches, would address this.
The four-arm switch (true) construct is unusual for this codebase; a plain if/else if chain would read more naturally and be easier to git blame.

hasAnySubscription and getActivePlanName are two very similar methods that always fire together, with getActivePlanName already implying whether an active subscription exists via a non-null return; hasAnySubscription only adds coverage for terminal/incomplete rows. A single query returning both activePlanName and hasAnySubscription would halve round-trips and remove a code path that is hard to keep in sync, making the current split feel like unnecessary API surface.

parseEnforcementStartsAt treats an empty string environment value as invalid (throwing) but an unset value as using the default, which is surprising behavior for operators who set ENTITLEMENTS_ENFORCEMENT_STARTS_AT= as an empty value in a .env file. Treating an empty string as unset (e.g., envValue?.trim() || undefined) would be more consistent with other keys in this file.
